l4_steps.name: Import approved pairings into rostering module
l4_steps.input: Approved crew pairing solution exported from CM-01 pairing optimisation
l4_steps.output: Pairing library loaded into rostering module for the bid period
l4_steps.kpi: 100% of approved pairings imported with zero data loss; import completed ≤2 hours after CM-01 sign-off
l4_steps.pain_point: Pairing handoff format mismatches between Jeppesen pairing and rostering modules cause silent truncation of augmented-crew flags — manual audit required for long-haul pairings

l4_steps.name: Configure bid period parameters and CBA rules
l4_steps.input: Flight schedule, collective bargaining agreement (CBA), bidding calendar, vacation approval list
l4_steps.output: Bid period configuration: dates, block-hour limits, vacation slots, trip-trade eligibility rules
l4_steps.kpi: Bid package published ≥21 days before period start per CBA; 0 rule-configuration errors at bid launch
l4_steps.pain_point: CBA rule amendments require manual reconfiguration of Jeppesen constraint tables — no automated ingestion from contract management system; misconfigurations discovered only when crew protests are filed

l4_steps.name: Validate crew qualification and fleet eligibility
l4_steps.system: Jeppesen Crew Management + Boeing Toolbox / CAMP
l4_steps.input: Crew qualification records, recurrent training schedule, expiry dates from training tracking system
l4_steps.output: Eligible crew list segmented by fleet type and seat position for bid period
l4_steps.kpi: 0 unqualified crew included in bid package; eligibility validation completed ≥25 days before period start
l4_steps.pain_point: Qualification expiry records in Boeing Toolbox / CAMP sync to Jeppesen with a 24–48-hour lag — risk of including crew whose type-rating or medical lapses within the bid window

l4_steps.name: Publish bid package to crew self-service portal
l4_steps.input: Finalized pairing library, bid period configuration, eligible crew list
l4_steps.output: Published bid package accessible to all eligible crew via CrewPortal and mobile app
l4_steps.kpi: Bid package live ≥21 days before bid close; 0 incorrect or duplicate pairings in published package
l4_steps.pain_point: Late schedule changes after bid publication require reissuing the full package, compressing crew bid time below the CBA-mandated minimum — triggers grievance filings and OCC planning disruption

l4_steps.name: Capture ranked bid preferences from crew members
l4_steps.input: Published bid package, personal scheduling preferences, personal rest requirements
l4_steps.output: Ranked preference list submitted per crew member; system timestamp of each submission
l4_steps.kpi: Bid submission rate ≥95% by deadline; average ranking depth ≥15 preferences per crew member
l4_steps.pain_point: Mobile app version fragmentation causes intermittent bid submission failures for crew on older devices — preference loss occurs without error confirmation, leading to unintended default-assignment triggers

l4_steps.name: Validate bid completeness and close bidding window
l4_steps.input: Submitted crew bids, bid deadline, CBA late-bid rules
l4_steps.output: Validated bid dataset; list of non-bidders flagged for reserve-rule default assignment
l4_steps.kpi: 100% bid validation completed within 2 hours of bid close; non-bidder list issued to planning team within 1 hour
l4_steps.pain_point: Non-bidders assigned by reserve default rules increase reserve utilisation pressure during high-absence periods (holidays, training blocks), reducing buffer for day-of-operations coverage

l4_steps.name: Run automated seniority-based bid award algorithm
l4_steps.input: Validated crew bids, seniority list, pairing library, block-hour limits per crew
l4_steps.output: Draft roster with bid awards allocated by seniority order; uncovered-pairing exception list
l4_steps.kpi: Automated award covers ≥85% of pairings without manual intervention; optimisation run completes <3 hours
l4_steps.pain_point: Seniority-driven award algorithm creates systematic clustering — junior crew receive chronically undesirable pairings, driving grievance filings and attrition at base cities with high seniority concentration

l4_steps.name: Apply FRMS fatigue constraints to draft roster
l4_steps.input: Draft roster, crew duty history for prior 90 days, rest period records
l4_steps.output: FRMS-validated roster with per-crew fatigue index scores; list of crew flagged above threshold
l4_steps.kpi: 0 crew assigned duties with predicted fatigue index >70 (Jeppesen FRMS 0–100 scale); FRMS validation completed <2 hours
l4_steps.pain_point: FRMS scoring relies on self-reported rest periods logged in CrewPortal — inaccurate entries produce false-compliant rosters that trigger FRMS alerts only on the day of operation when it is too late to rebalance

l4_steps.name: Check FAR Part 117 duty and rest compliance
l4_steps.input: FRMS-validated draft roster, FAR Part 117 / EASA FTL rule set, augmented-crew designation flags
l4_steps.output: Compliance report per crew member; list of FAR Part 117 violations with step-number reference
l4_steps.kpi: 0 FAR Part 117 violations in roster at publication; compliance check completed <4 hours
l4_steps.pain_point: Augmented-crew provisions under FAR Part 117 §117.21 are not fully parameterised in Jeppesen — ultra-long-range pairings require manual override and legal review, adding 24–48 hours to the rostering cycle

l4_steps.name: Resolve uncovered pairings via reserve assignment
l4_steps.input: Uncovered pairing list, qualified reserve crew availability, CBA reserve-call rules
l4_steps.output: Fully covered draft roster with reserve assignments documented; updated reserve utilisation report
l4_steps.kpi: 0 uncovered pairings at draft finalisation; reserve utilisation ≤30% of available reserve pool
l4_steps.pain_point: Reserve pool insufficiency during peak holiday bid periods forces voluntary overtime — CBA premium-pay triggers create budget variance of up to 15% above planned crew cost in Q4

l4_steps.name: Review and adjudicate crew bid award protests
l4_steps.input: Crew grievance and protest submissions, draft roster, CBA seniority and award rules
l4_steps.output: Adjudicated roster with documented award rationale per disputed assignment
l4_steps.kpi: 100% of bid protests resolved within 5 business days per CBA; protest rate <2% of total crew bids
l4_steps.pain_point: Seniority disputes requiring CBA interpretation escalate to labor relations, extending resolution timelines and delaying roster finalisation — unresolved protests at publication date force provisional assignments

l4_steps.name: Incorporate pre-approved trip trades and swaps
l4_steps.input: Pre-approved trip trade requests, adjudicated roster, qualification matrix
l4_steps.output: Updated roster with pre-period swaps incorporated; qualification validation report for all traded duties
l4_steps.kpi: Trip trade approval cycle ≤48 hours; 0 qualification violations resulting from approved trades
l4_steps.pain_point: Trip trades approved outside Jeppesen via email bypass the system's built-in qualification check — latent safety risk discovered only at crew sign-in when crew tracking flags the mismatch

l4_steps.name: Obtain final compliance sign-off and lock roster
l4_steps.system: Jeppesen Crew Management + AWS S3 / Redshift (compliance audit log)
l4_steps.input: Final roster, FAR Part 117 compliance report, FRMS validation summary
l4_steps.output: Signed compliance certificate; roster record locked against further edits; audit log entry written to AWS data lake
l4_steps.kpi: Compliance sign-off completed ≥5 days before period start; 0 open violations at sign-off
l4_steps.pain_point: Compliance audit trail stored in a separate AWS S3/Redshift data lake has no direct linkage to the Jeppesen roster record — reconstructing evidence for FAA audit queries requires manual correlation across two systems

l4_steps.name: Publish final roster and notify crew via portal
l4_steps.system: Jeppesen Crew Management (CrewPortal) + airline push-notification service
l4_steps.input: Locked compliant roster, crew contact preferences
l4_steps.output: Published roster visible in CrewPortal; push notifications sent to crew mobile devices; acknowledgment tracking open
l4_steps.kpi: 100% of crew notified within 1 hour of publication; crew acknowledgment rate ≥90% within 48 hours of release
l4_steps.pain_point: Push-notification delivery rates drop to ~70% for crew on international layovers with low cellular connectivity — crew risk missing roster start dates, forcing manual telephone outreach by crew scheduling

l4_steps.name: Distribute final roster data feed to OCC
l4_steps.system: Jeppesen Crew Management + SITA Airport Management System (AMS)
l4_steps.output: Crew roster data feed ingested by OCC systems; gate and stand planning inputs updated with crew assignments
l4_steps.kpi: Roster data available in OCC within 30 minutes of publication; 0 data-sync errors in first 24 hours
l4_steps.pain_point: Roster-to-OCC data feed uses legacy SFTP batch transfer rather than a real-time API — the resulting 30-minute lag means OCC operates on stale crew assignments during the handoff window, creating conflict risk for back-to-back duty pairings
